barriers.reason: The patient has no car, relies on two buses each way to a distant unit with only a 3 PM chair, leaves by 1:30 PM and does not get home until about 8:30 PM, and is already skipping sessions because of this burden.

alternatives.text: Message the dialysis unit social worker to help with transport arrangements and benefits screening.
Ask the dialysis unit for a later chair time or a different day that matches an available ride; frame as a request given limited chair times.

If the patient cannot use fixed-route buses, apply for ADA Paratransit certification (Northern Illinois Transit Authority, 312-663-HELP); note certification is not immediate and rides run only when fixed-route service runs.

barriers.reason: The patient eats mostly corner-store chips and lunch meat, the real grocery is a bus ride away, and they are too wiped out after dialysis to shop, making fresh low-potassium produce hard to obtain.

alternatives.text: Ask the dialysis unit dietitian to rebuild the renal diet around foods the patient can actually obtain, including corner-store and pantry options.
Use the Greater Chicago Food Depository locator to find pantries open on non-treatment days, and pair pantry use with renal-dietitian guidance since pantry food is often not renal-friendly.
Apply for SNAP through Illinois ABE (abe.illinois.gov); very low-income households may qualify for expedited benefits within seven days.

barriers.reason: The patient is reluctant about another trip downtown and already struggles to reach appointments by bus; adding a separate fistula-visit trip compounds the established transport burden.

alternatives.text: Schedule the fistula check on the same day/campus as an existing dialysis visit, or use telehealth if a physical exam is not required.
Ask the dialysis unit social worker to help arrange transport and benefits for the surgery referral.
If fixed-route bus use is prevented by health, apply for ADA Paratransit certification; note it is not immediate and only runs when fixed-route service runs.
